title: Critical-mineral ownership on federal lands can be strategically relevant while foreign-parent visibility and supply-chain control remain incomplete
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-27-108094 review of foreign investment in critical-mineral mining on federal lands
geography: United States federal lands, hardrock mining claimants and operators, and critical-mineral supply chains involving foreign parent entities

observations.period: February 2026 federal-land plan count, 2019–2025 export context, and October 6, 2026 GAO report publicly released October 16

denominator.unit: claimants and operators associated with critical-mineral mines on federal lands whose ownership information GAO reviewed

approved_federal_land_plans.unit: approved hardrock mining plans of operation on federal land as of February 2026

ownership_determined.unit: claimants or operators out of 43 for which GAO determined ownership information

foreign_subsidiaries.unit: companies in the 32-company ownership set that were subsidiaries of foreign entities

chinese_financial_interest.value: at least two cases in which Chinese entities had financial interests in the foreign parent companies; GAO found none of the 14 foreign subsidiaries had Chinese-owned parent companies

disclosure_requirement.value: the 1872 Mining Law does not require BLM or Forest Service to collect foreign-parent information or require claimants or operators to submit foreign-ownership information; a U.S. subsidiary can serve as claimant for a foreign business
disclosure_requirement.unit: reported federal-land information and eligibility condition

supply_chain_constraints.value: critical-mineral supply chains face substantial capital needs and limited domestic processing capacity; the United States exports large quantities of domestically extracted ore to Canada, Mexico, China, and other countries

foreign_investment_review.value: the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States can review foreign investment in mining when it relates to potential national-security concerns

control_conversion.unit: beneficial control, mine production, processing, export destination, investment approval, disruption, domestic availability, local employment, environmental impact, or national-security outcome

observations.method: Structured extraction from GAO-27-108094, based on ownership information from multiple sources for 43 claimants and operators, federal laws, agency processes, interviews with officials, and analysis of critical-mineral exports from 2019 through 2025. Plan counts, ownership determination, foreign subsidiaries, Chinese interests, disclosure rules, supply-chain conditions, review authority, and control outcomes are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: Ownership could not be determined for 11 of the 43 reviewed claimants or operators, and a foreign subsidiary does not by itself establish beneficial control, operational direction, Chinese control, or national-security harm. Export quantities, ownership information, and agency review authorities do not establish mine-level production, processing, disruption, or domestic supply outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Federal-land mining claimants and operators, workers and communities near mines, downstream manufacturers, federal land managers, and households affected by critical-mineral prices, security, or environmental tradeoffs.
observations.counterinterpretation: Foreign investment can supply capital and technical capacity, and financial interest is not equivalent to ownership or control; domestic processing and supply-chain resilience may improve through multiple firms and allied trade even when federal ownership records are incomplete.

related_sources.claim: The official accessible report contains the federal-land mining, ownership, foreign-investment, export, and agency-authority findings.
GAO identifies a related report on BLM's role in collecting citizenship information from mining claimants.

boundary: This record advances a bounded federal-land critical-mineral ownership-to-geoeconomic-dependence route. It does not establish beneficial control, mine production, processing, export destination at the mine level, CFIUS action, disruption, domestic availability, local employment, environmental impact, or national-security outcome.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Canonical GAO product URL string used as a stable source identifier; accessible report and related report links are retained for reproduction.
